business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (10-K Item 1)
business_model.claim: GEO owns, leases and manages secure facilities, processing centers and reentry facilities, and provides community-based services in the United States, Australia and South Africa.
quotes: We specialize in the ownership, leasing and management of secure facilities, processing centers and reentry facilities and the provision of community-based services in the United States, Australia and South Africa.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited items (10-K Items 1 and 1A)
business_model.claim: Its customers are government agencies, and it relies on a limited number of them.

The loss of, or a significant decrease in revenues from, our limited number of customers could seriously harm our financial condition and results of operations.

business_model.claim: Services are delivered at facilities GEO owns, at facilities it leases and at government-owned facilities, the last under managed-only contracts.
quotes: our services are provided at facilities which we either own, lease or are owned by our government agency partners.

business_model.claim: GEO reports four segments: U.S. Secure Services, Electronic Monitoring and Supervision Services, Reentry Services and International Services.
quotes: We conduct our business through four reportable business segments: our U.S. Secure Services segment; our Electronic Monitoring and Supervision Services segment; our Reentry Services segment and our International Services segment.

business_model.claim: Secure Services revenue depends on per diem rates and compensated mandays. Occupancy is measured as compensated mandays as a share of capacity.
quotes: The per diem rates that we charge our clients often vary by contract across our portfolio.
The average occupancy is calculated by taking compensated mandays as a percentage of capacity.

business_model.claim: U.S. Secure Services compensated mandays rose from about 16.6 million in 2024 to 17.2 million in 2025. Average occupancy, excluding idle facilities, rose from 86.6% to 88.7%.
quotes: The number of compensated mandays in U.S. Secure Services facilities was approximately 17.2 million in 2025 and 16.6 million in 2024.
The average occupancy in our U.S. Secure Services facilities was 88.7% and 86.6% of capacity in 2025 and 2024, respectively, excluding idle facilities.

business_model.claim: U.S. Secure Services revenue grew $222.6 million in 2025. New contract activations added $152.4 million, and contract terminations took away about $51.1 million.
quotes: Revenues for U.S. Secure Services increased by $222.6 million in 2025 compared to 2024 due to aggregate net increases of $152.4 million related to the activations of our new contracts at our company-owned Delaney Hall, North Lake and D. Ray James facilities as well as our managed-only contract at the North Florida Detention Center and new transportation contracts.
Partially offsetting these increases were decreases of approximately $51.1 million related to contract terminations.

business_model.claim: Higher occupancies, transportation services, rates and per diem amounts added a further $121.3 million to U.S. Secure Services revenue in 2025.
quotes: We also experienced an aggregate net increase of $121.3 million due to increases in occupancies, transportation services, rates and/or per diem amounts in connection with contract modifications.

business_model.claim: Electronic Monitoring revenue depends on participant counts under ICE's ISAP program. It fell $11.9 million in 2025 because average participant counts declined.
quotes: Revenues for Electronic Monitoring and Supervision Services decreased by $11.9 million in 2025 compared to 2024 primarily due to decreases in average participant counts under the Intensive Supervision and Appearance Program ("ISAP").

On September 30, 2025, we announced that we entered into a two-year contract with ICE for the continued provision of electronic monitoring, case management and supervision services under the Intensive Supervision and Appearance Program ("ISAP").

business_model.claim: Reentry Services revenue grew $9.0 million in 2025, mainly from $6.9 million of new day reporting center contracts.
quotes: Revenues for Reentry Services increased by $9.0 million in 2025 compared to 2024 primarily due to increases of $6.9 million due to new day reporting center contracts.

business_model.claim: International Services revenue fell by a net $14.6 million in 2025, mainly because the Junee contract in Australia transitioned to the government.
quotes: We experienced a net decrease of $14.6 million primarily due to the transition of our managed-only contract for the Junee Correctional Centre in Australia to the government effective March 31, 2025.
